title: Security review: audit events + permissions for route-level A/B experiments
creator: Dylan Brooks
content:
Context
- Feature: Route-level A/B testing in Console (create/validate/start/stop/rollback experiments that deterministically split traffic by route).
- This ticket covers: (1) RBAC/permissions model, (2) audit event coverage + payload requirements, (3) abuse scenarios + mitigations.
- Goal: satisfy Security minimums for beta enablement (Hosted + Dedicated) and avoid “silent traffic shifting”.

References
- Confluence: sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/ab-testing-audit-events.json
- ADR (privacy/exposure logs): sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-0188-experiment-exposure-logging-and-privacy.json
- Console CRUD work: ENG-2843 / PR redwood/pr_18426_console-backend-experiment-crud-endpoints.json
- Audit log implementation: PR redwood/pr_18473_audit-log-events-for-experiment-lifecycle.json
- Beta flag / entitlements: ENG-2848 / PR redwood/pr_18491_feature-flag-console-ab-testing-beta.json

Scope
A) Permission model (Console + API)
1) Actions requiring explicit permissions
- Create experiment (draft)
- Update experiment config (while draft or paused)
- Validate experiment config
- Start experiment (begins traffic shifting)
- Pause/Stop experiment
- Rollback experiment (traffic back to control)
- Delete experiment (draft-only for beta; no delete after start)
- Export results / download report (if present in beta)

2) Proposed RBAC mapping (initial)
- New permission: experiments:write (create/update/validate)
- New permission: experiments:run (start/stop/rollback)
- New permission: experiments:read (view configs + results)
- Admin override: org:admin implicitly includes experiments:* (consistent with existing rollouts policy)

3) Role guidance (Console UI)
- Project Admin: experiments:write + experiments:run
- Project Developer: experiments:read (and optionally experiments:write for some tiers)
- Read-only / Analyst: experiments:read (results only), but cannot see raw assignment keys / hashing inputs

4) Service accounts / API keys
- API keys used for calling inference routes MUST NOT automatically gain experiments:run.
- Only Console control-plane actions (human user or privileged automation account) can change experiment state.
- If we support automation: require a dedicated “experiment-admin” service account type and restrict to allowlisted IPs / SSO-only creation.

5) Tenant isolation / resource scoping
- All experiment operations scoped to: organization_id + project_id.
- Route-level scoping: explicit route_id (or route pattern) must be within the project.
- Dedicated: ensure isolation between tenants sharing a Dedicated pool (no cross-tenant reads on results).

Open questions (needs Security sign-off)
- Do we require 2-person approval for start/rollback in enterprise orgs? (Non-goal for v1 but may be requested by prospects.)
- Should “start” require re-auth (password/SSO prompt) for users with SSO? (Probably overkill for beta; consider as future hardening.)

B) Audit logging requirements
1) Required lifecycle events (must be emitted)
- ab_experiment.created
- ab_experiment.updated
- ab_experiment.validated (optional but preferred; helps trace why start was blocked)
- ab_experiment.started
- ab_experiment.paused
- ab_experiment.stopped
- ab_experiment.rolled_back
- ab_experiment.deleted (draft-only; if we prohibit delete post-start, enforce and log attempted delete as denied)
- ab_experiment.permission_denied (recommended): when experiments:run/write actions are attempted without permission

2) Required audit fields (minimum payload)
- event_name
- occurred_at (UTC)
- actor_type (user | service_account)
- actor_id
- actor_email (if user)
- actor_ip
- actor_user_agent
- organization_id
- project_id
- environment (hosted | dedicated | private) + region
- experiment_id
- experiment_name
- route (normalized route identifier, NOT raw URL with query params)
- change_summary (human-readable)
- diff (structured diff is ideal, but for beta at least include: fields_changed list + old/new for traffic split + variants)
- request_id / trace_id for correlation

3) Data minimization / PII constraints
- Do NOT log prompts, completions, headers, user_id values, raw hashing inputs.
- Do NOT log full model config blobs if they may include customer secrets (e.g., tool schemas with proprietary names). Log model identifiers + high-level config (temperature, max_tokens) only.
- For variants: include variant_id + pinned model_version_id; avoid including “routing rules” that embed customer-specific identifiers.

4) Retention and access
- Audit logs should follow existing audit logging retention by plan (Enterprise default: 1 year; others: 30–90 days).
- Access: org admins + security/auditor roles; ensure results viewers cannot see sensitive audit payloads beyond change_summary.
- SIEM export: confirm ab_experiment.* events flow through the standard export path (Kevin Osei to verify).

C) Abuse scenarios + mitigations
1) Unauthorized traffic shifting (primary risk)
Scenario
- A user with basic project access starts an experiment and routes 50–100% traffic to an unapproved model variant, causing cost/latency spikes or compliance violations.
Mitigations
- Separate experiments:write vs experiments:run.
- Default deny experiments:run to non-admin roles.
- Console shows explicit warning modal on Start: “This will shift production traffic for route X; requires experiments:run; recorded in audit logs.”
- Optional guardrail: enforce max initial split for first start (e.g., <=10%) unless org has “allow_high_risk_changes” entitlement.

2) Circumventing rollout/fallback safety
Scenario
- User configures an experiment that masks fallback policies or effectively disables canary protections.
Mitigations
- Enforce routing precedence rules from ADR-0187/0188 in policy engine (experiments must not disable fallbacks; reliability routing always applies).
- Audit log captures effective policy precedence summary at start (e.g., “fallbacks active: true; canary overlap: blocked/allowed”).

3) Privilege escalation via experiment mutation
Scenario
- User with experiments:write edits an already-started experiment to change split from 5% to 95% without the “start” action.
Mitigations
- Treat split changes on a running experiment as experiments:run (or block updates while running; require pause -> edit -> restart).
- Emit ab_experiment.updated with explicit old/new split values.

4) High-cardinality / log injection
Scenario
- Attacker sets experiment name/variant label to include control characters or unique IDs to explode metrics cardinality / break dashboards.
Mitigations
- Validate experiment_name and variant_name (length limit, allowed charset, strip control chars).
- Canonical “variant_id” is server-generated; UI labels are display-only and excluded from metric tags.
- Metrics allowlist for tags enforced (see PR redwood/pr_18519_reduce-metric-cardinality-experiment-tags.json; ensure consistent).

5) Data exfiltration via audit logs / results export
Scenario
- A user without permission exports results or views audit changes that reveal sensitive model configs or eval prompt sets.
Mitigations
- experiments:read is required for results; eval suite attachment requires evals:read and experiments:read.
- Audit payload is sanitized (no prompt set contents, only eval_suite_id + name).
- Export endpoints check permissions and are audited (ab_experiment.results_exported).

6) Replay/debug endpoints leaking assignment keys
Scenario
- Support tooling allows replaying assignment decisions by providing hashing inputs, which may include PII.
Mitigations
- No public or customer-facing “explain assignment” endpoint in beta.
- Any internal debug tooling must accept only sanitized identifiers and require elevated internal permissions; also audited.

Acceptance Criteria
- [RBAC] experiments:write / experiments:run / experiments:read are implemented in Console backend and enforced on all CRUD + lifecycle endpoints.
- [RBAC] Split changes on running experiment are disallowed OR gated by experiments:run (document final decision).
- [Audit] All lifecycle events listed above are emitted with required fields; payload contains NO prompts/completions/raw request headers/raw hashing inputs.
- [Audit] Permission denied attempts for experiments:run/write are logged (or justified if we choose not to).
- [Audit] SIEM export path includes ab_experiment.* (confirm with Kevin Osei).
- [Docs] Security notes added to internal DevEx guide and runbook links updated.

Implementation notes / where to add checks
- Console backend: middleware to map roles -> permissions (Chloe Martin)
- Audit event emitter: consolidated helper in Console backend (ensure consistent field naming across events)
- Gateway: exposure logs are separate; do not confuse with audit logs (exposure logs are analytics; audit logs are admin actions)

Comments / Updates
2026-02-10 (Marcus Lin)
- Initial pass: overall direction OK. Biggest gap: updating split while experiment running must be treated as “run” permission (or require pause). Also strongly recommend logging permission denied events for experiments:run.
- Please confirm we are not logging user_id header or API key id as audit fields. Those belong in internal tracing, not audit.

2026-02-12 (Chloe Martin)
- Implemented: block updates to split/variants while status=RUNNING; requires PAUSE first (PR upcoming). Added validation on experiment_name charset/length. Will follow up on permission denied logging.

2026-02-18 (Kevin Osei)
- SIEM: ab_experiment.* will be included automatically if it uses the standard audit pipeline category “console_admin”. Ensure event_name prefix matches allowlist (ab_experiment.).

2026-02-21 (Dylan Brooks)
- Beta gating depends on sign-off here + SRE guardrails. Please review the final audit payload fields in PR redwood/pr_18473_audit-log-events-for-experiment-lifecycle.json and confirm OK to proceed to beta enablement (ENG-2848).
